summary.en: Sogdian Marakanda, taken by Alexander, grew into the hub of Silk Road trade, was destroyed by Genghis Khan in 1220 and rebuilt by Timur as his imperial capital, whose Registan and mausolea are among the masterpieces of Islamic architecture.
summary.zh: 粟特的马拉坎达曾被亚历山大攻占，后发展为丝绸之路贸易的枢纽；1220年被成吉思汗摧毁，又被帖木儿重建为帝国都城，其雷吉斯坦广场和诸陵墓是伊斯兰建筑的杰作。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List: Samarkand – Crossroad of Cultures
History of Civilizations of Central Asia, vol. IV (UNESCO)

name.zh: 布哈拉（努米杰卡特，安国）

polity.zh: 倭马亚王朝，后为阿拔斯王朝

布哈拉人民苏维埃共和国

summary.en: Capital of the Samanids and a famed centre of Islamic learning—Ibn Sina studied in its library—Bukhara survived the Mongol sack to become seat of the Shaybanid khans and the emirs of Bukhara until the Red Army took it in 1920.
summary.zh: 布哈拉是萨曼王朝的都城和著名的伊斯兰学术中心（伊本·西那曾在其图书馆求学），经蒙古洗劫后复兴，成为昔班尼汗国和布哈拉埃米尔的都城，直至1920年被红军攻占。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List: Historic Centre of Bukhara
Richard N. Frye, Bukhara: The Medieval Achievement (1965)

polity.zh: 俄罗斯帝国（1918年起苏维埃）

polity.zh: 苏联（哈萨克自治共和国首都，1936年起哈萨克苏维埃社会主义共和国首都）

summary.en: Founded as the Russian fort of Verny in 1854 below the Zailiysky Alatau, the town became Alma-Ata in 1921 and capital of Soviet Kazakhstan from 1929; it remained the capital of independent Kazakhstan until 1997 and is still its largest city.
summary.zh: 1854年俄国在外伊犁阿拉套山下建立维尔内要塞，1921年改名阿拉木图，1929年起为苏联哈萨克的首府；独立后的哈萨克斯坦以其为首都直至1997年，至今仍是该国最大城市。

sources.title: Martha Brill Olcott, The Kazakhs, 2nd ed. (1995)

polity.zh: 地方王公（先后臣属康居、突厥）

summary.en: The oasis of Chach (Chinese Shi, “stone”) on the Chirchik became Tashkent (“stone city”) under the Karakhanids. Taken by Kokand and then by Russia in 1865, it served as capital of Russian Turkestan and is now Uzbekistan’s capital and Central Asia’s largest city.
summary.zh: 奇尔奇克河畔的赭时绿洲（汉文称“石国”）在喀喇汗时期称为塔什干（意为“石城”）。先后为浩罕和俄国（1865年）所占，曾为俄属突厥斯坦首府，今为乌兹别克斯坦首都和中亚最大城市。

sources.title: Jeff Sahadeo, Russian Colonial Society in Tashkent, 1865–1923 (2007)

note: Early name periods and polities are simplified; between 1500 and 1809 control shifted repeatedly.

modern.zh: 梅尔夫（土库曼斯坦马雷附近）

苏联（土库曼苏维埃社会主义共和国）

summary.en: Successive walled cities in the Murghab oasis made Merv a capital of Khurasan, the launch-point of the Abbasid revolution in 747 and Sanjar’s Seljuk seat. Destroyed by the Mongols in 1221, its ruins lie beside the Russian-founded town of Mary.
summary.zh: 穆尔加布绿洲上相继兴建的城池使梅尔夫成为呼罗珊的首府、747年阿拔斯革命的发源地以及桑贾尔的塞尔柱都城。1221年遭蒙古摧毁，其遗址位于俄国人建立的马雷城旁。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List: State Historical and Cultural Park “Ancient Merv”

note: The QID is the archaeological site; the modern city of Mary (Q5713, founded 1884, renamed 1937) lies c. 30 km west.

polity.zh: 喀尔喀蒙古（1691年起属清朝）

summary.en: Genghis Khan chose the Orkhon valley site in 1220 and Ögedei walled it in 1235 as the imperial capital, visited by envoys such as William of Rubruck. After Ming troops destroyed it in 1388, the Erdene Zuu monastery rose from its stones in 1585.
summary.zh: 成吉思汗于1220年选定鄂尔浑河谷此地，窝阔台于1235年筑城定为帝国都城，鲁布鲁克等使节曾到访。1388年被明军摧毁后，1585年人们以其石料修建了额尔德尼召寺。

sources.title: William of Rubruck, The Mission of Friar William of Rubruck, tr. Peter Jackson (1990)
UNESCO World Heritage List: Orkhon Valley Cultural Landscape

note: The 1220 founding follows Wikidata; the city walls date from 1235.

polity.zh: 苏联（哈萨克苏维埃社会主义共和国）
哈萨克斯坦（1997年12月10日起为首都）

summary.en: A Cossack outpost founded in 1830 on the Ishim, Akmolinsk became Tselinograd, hub of the Virgin Lands campaign, in 1961. Renamed Akmola and then Astana (“capital”), it replaced Almaty as Kazakhstan’s capital in 1997; it was called Nur-Sultan from 2019 to 2022.
summary.zh: 1830年哥萨克在伊希姆河畔建立阿克莫林斯克要塞，1961年更名切利诺格勒，成为垦荒运动的中心。后改名阿克莫拉，再改为阿斯塔纳（意为“首都”），1997年取代阿拉木图成为哈萨克斯坦首都；2019年至2022年曾称努尔苏丹。

sources.title: Adeeb Khalid, Central Asia: A New History from the Imperial Conquests to the Present (2021)

polity.en: Soviet Union (capital of Kirghiz ASSR, from 1936 Kirghiz SSR)
polity.zh: 苏联（吉尔吉斯自治共和国首府，1936年起吉尔吉斯苏维埃社会主义共和国首都）

summary.en: The Kokand fortress of Pishpek in the Chu valley was destroyed by Russian troops in 1862 and replaced by a settler town. Renamed Frunze after the Bolshevik commander born there, it became capital of Soviet Kyrgyzstan and took the name Bishkek in 1991.
summary.zh: 楚河谷地的浩罕要塞皮什佩克于1862年被俄军摧毁，其旁兴起移民城镇。后以生于此地的布尔什维克将领伏龙芝之名命名，成为苏联吉尔吉斯的首府，1991年改名比什凯克。

sources.title: Adeeb Khalid, Central Asia: A New History from the Imperial Conquests to the Present (2021)

polity.en: Soviet Union (Bukharan PSR; capital of Tajik ASSR from 1924)
polity.zh: 苏联（布哈拉人民苏维埃共和国；1924年起为塔吉克自治共和国首府）
苏联（塔吉克苏维埃社会主义共和国）
苏联（塔吉克苏维埃社会主义共和国）

summary.en: Named after its Monday (dushanbe) market, the village in the Hisor valley was made capital of Soviet Tajikistan in 1924, renamed Stalinabad in 1929, and regained the name Dushanbe in 1961 during de-Stalinisation.
summary.zh: 杜尚别得名于每逢周一（塔吉克语“杜尚别”）的集市，这个希萨尔谷地的村落于1924年成为苏联塔吉克的首府，1929年改名斯大林纳巴德，1961年非斯大林化时恢复原名。

sources.title: Adeeb Khalid, Central Asia: A New History from the Imperial Conquests to the Present (2021)

note: The village is older than 1785; the first range begins with the Emirate of Bukhara.

summary.en: Founded in 1639 as the mobile monastery-camp (örgöö) of the Buddhist leader Zanabazar, it settled on the Tuul river in 1778 and became the capital of independent Mongolia in 1911; it was renamed Ulaanbaatar, “Red Hero”, in 1924.
summary.zh: 1639年作为佛教领袖扎那巴扎尔的移动寺院营地（乌尔格）而建立，1778年定居于土拉河畔，1911年成为独立蒙古的首都；1924年改名乌兰巴托，意为“红色英雄”。

sources.title: Charles R. Bawden, The Modern History of Mongolia (1968)

polity.en: Afghanistan (republics, then the Islamic Emirate from 1996–2001 and 2021)
polity.zh: 阿富汗（共和国时期，1996—2001年及2021年起为伊斯兰酋长国）

summary.en: Set in a high valley on the routes between the Oxus lands and India, Kabul was a Shahi royal seat, Babur’s first kingdom and, from 1776, the Durrani and Barakzai capital; it has been the capital of every Afghan regime since, and was fought over in the Anglo-Afghan wars and the civil war of the 1990s.
summary.zh: 喀布尔坐落在阿姆河流域通往印度道路上的高山谷地，曾是沙希王朝的王都和巴布尔的第一个王国，1776年起为杜兰尼与巴拉克扎伊王朝的都城；此后历届阿富汗政权均以此为首都，英阿战争和1990年代内战中屡遭争夺。

sources.title: Thomas J. Barfield, Afghanistan: A Cultural and Political History (2010)

summary.en: The oasis city of the Hari river was a Persian and then Islamic provincial centre, was devastated by the Mongols, revived under the Kart kings and reached its height as the Timurid capital of Shah Rukh and Husayn Bayqara, when Gawhar Shad, Navoi, Jami and Bihzad made it the cultural capital of the Persianate world.
summary.zh: 赫拉特是哈里河畔的绿洲城市，先后为波斯和伊斯兰的地方中心，遭蒙古人摧毁后在卡尔特王朝治下复兴，作为沙哈鲁和忽辛·拜哈拉的帖木儿王朝都城达到鼎盛，高哈尔·沙德、纳沃伊、贾米和毕扎德使其成为波斯文化世界的文化之都。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica: Herat ii. History, Medieval Period

note: Rule over Herat changed hands many times between Safavids, Uzbeks and Afghans; the periods given are simplified.

summary.en: Ancient Bactra, the “mother of cities”, was a Kushan centre and a great Buddhist city whose Nava Vihara monastery Xuanzang visited, then a leading city of Islamic Khurasan and the home of the poet Rumi’s family. Genghis Khan razed it in 1220, and after the 1860s Mazar-i Sharif nearby replaced it as the region’s capital.
summary.zh: 古代的巴克特拉号称“众城之母”，曾是贵霜的中心和佛教重镇，玄奘到过其纳缚僧伽蓝；后来成为伊斯兰呼罗珊的名城，诗人鲁米的家族即来自这里。1220年被成吉思汗夷平，1860年代后附近的马扎里沙里夫取代它成为地区首府。

note: Early boundaries between the Yuezhi and Kushan periods and between Hunnic dynasties are approximate.

polity.zh: 阿富汗（共和国时期，1996—2001年及2021年起为伊斯兰酋长国）

summary.en: The chief city of the southern Afghan plains guarded the road from Iran to India, so the Mughals and Safavids fought over it for two centuries. Mirwais Hotak’s revolt here in 1709 began the Afghan conquest of Iran, and Ahmad Shah Durrani built a new city as his capital; it remained the heartland of the Durrani Pashtuns and, later, of the Taliban.
summary.zh: 坎大哈是阿富汗南部平原的首要城市，扼守从伊朗到印度的道路，莫卧儿和萨法维为此争夺了两个世纪。1709年米尔维斯·霍塔克在此起事，开启阿富汗人征服伊朗之路；艾哈迈德沙·杜兰尼在此新建都城。这里始终是杜兰尼普什图人、后来也是塔利班的腹地。

sources.title: Thomas J. Barfield, Afghanistan: A Cultural and Political History (2010)

note: Rulers before about 1000 CE are poorly documented; the Zunbils held the region against the Arabs until the Saffarids.

summary.en: At the mouth of the Fergana valley on the Syr Darya, Khujand grew from the farthest city founded by Alexander. Its governor Timur Malik held out against the Mongols in 1220; Russia took it in 1866, and as Soviet Leninabad it was the industrial and political base of Tajikistan’s ruling elite.
summary.zh: 苦盏位于锡尔河畔费尔干纳谷地的入口，由亚历山大所建最远的城市发展而来。1220年其守将帖木儿·灭里抵抗蒙古人；1866年俄国攻占此城，苏联时期称列宁纳巴德，是塔吉克斯坦执政精英的工业和政治基地。

sources.title: Yuri Bregel, An Historical Atlas of Central Asia (2003)

note: The identification of Khujand with Alexandria Eschate is widely accepted but not certain. The reversion to Khujand is dated 1991 or 1992.

土库曼苏维埃社会主义共和国（苏联）

summary.en: Founded as a Russian fort beside a Teke Turkmen village in 1881, after the storming of Geok Tepe, the town grew as a stop on the Transcaspian railway. Renamed Poltoratsk after a Bolshevik commissar, it became the capital of Soviet Turkmenistan, was flattened by the earthquake of 1948 and was rebuilt in white marble after independence.
summary.zh: 1881年格奥克捷佩被攻破后，俄国在一个帖克土库曼村落旁建起要塞，小城随外里海铁路而成长。它曾以一位布尔什维克人民委员的名字改称波尔托拉茨克，成为苏维埃土库曼的首都，1948年毁于大地震，独立后以白色大理石重建。

sources.title: Adrienne Lynn Edgar, Tribal Nation: The Making of Soviet Turkmenistan (2004)

note: Nearby Nisa was an early Parthian royal seat; the modern city dates from 1881.

polity.zh: 哈萨克自治共和国，后为哈萨克苏维埃社会主义共和国（苏联）

summary.en: A Kokand fort on the lower Syr Darya, Ak-Mechet was stormed by General Perovsky in 1853 and renamed after him, becoming a base for the Russian advance on Tashkent. Renamed Kzyl-Orda, “Red Capital”, it was the capital of Soviet Kazakhstan from 1925 until the seat moved to Alma-Ata in 1929.
summary.zh: 阿克麦切特原是浩罕汗国在锡尔河下游的堡垒，1853年被彼罗夫斯基将军攻占并以其名命名，成为俄国进军塔什干的基地。后改名克孜勒奥尔达，意为“红色首都”，1925年至1929年首府迁往阿拉木图之前是苏维埃哈萨克的首都。

note: The Kokand fort is dated 1817 or 1820 (Wikidata: 1820).

name.zh: 塞米巴拉金斯克（阿拉什城）

polity.en: Kazakh ASSR, then Kazakh SSR (Soviet Union)
polity.zh: 哈萨克自治共和国，后为哈萨克苏维埃社会主义共和国（苏联）

summary.en: Founded in 1718 as a Russian fort on the Irtysh near the ruins of a Buddhist monastery (the “seven palaces” of its name), Semipalatinsk was Dostoevsky’s place of exile, Abai’s market town and the seat of the Alash Orda government. From 1949 to 1989 the Soviet nuclear test site lay to its west.
summary.zh: 塞米巴拉金斯克于1718年作为俄国要塞建于额尔齐斯河畔，邻近一座佛寺遗址（地名意为“七座宫殿”）。这里是陀思妥耶夫斯基的流放地、阿拜常去的集镇和阿拉什自治政府的驻地。1949年至1989年，苏联核试验场就在其西面。

note: The Alash government’s control was nominal and contested by Whites and Reds; Bolsheviks held the city from late 1919.

polity.zh: 回民起事者，后为哲德沙尔

polity.en: People’s Republic of China (Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region)
polity.zh: 中华人民共和国（新疆维吾尔自治区）

summary.en: A pasture on the northern slope of the Tian Shan (its Mongolic name means “beautiful pasture”), Ürümqi became a walled Qing garrison town, Dihua, after the destruction of the Zunghars. It was the capital of Xinjiang province from 1884 and the base of the warlord governors of the republican era.
summary.zh: 乌鲁木齐原是天山北麓的一片牧场（其蒙古语名意为“优美的牧场”），准噶尔覆灭后成为清朝筑城驻军的迪化。1884年起为新疆省会，民国时期是新疆军阀督办的大本营。

sources.title: James A. Millward, Eurasian Crossroads: A History of Xinjiang (2007)

note: The Qing walled town was built in 1763 and the name Dihua was given in 1773; the name reverted to Ürümqi in 1954.

polity.en: Former Liang and other Hexi states
Contested by Tibet and the Uyghurs
Uyghur idiquts under the Mongol Empire
polity.zh: 蒙古帝国治下的畏兀儿亦都护

summary.en: The mud-brick capital of the Turfan oasis was a Chinese garrison, then a kingdom whose ruler Qu Wentai hosted Xuanzang in 630, then a Tang prefecture and the royal city of the Qocho Uyghurs. Abandoned after the Chagatayid wars of the 14th century, its ruins yielded the Manichaean and Buddhist manuscripts carried to Berlin by the German Turfan expeditions.
summary.zh: 这座吐鲁番绿洲的夯土都城先是汉人戍所，后为高昌国——其国王麴文泰于630年款待玄奘——再成为唐朝的西州和高昌回鹘的王城。十四世纪察合台汗国战乱后被废弃，其遗址出土的摩尼教和佛教写本被德国吐鲁番探险队带往柏林。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List: Silk Roads – the Routes Network of Chang’an-Tianshan Corridor
Valerie Hansen, The Silk Road: A New History (2012)

note: The garrison is dated to 48 BCE in Han sources. The period between Tang loss of Xizhou and Uyghur control (c. 790–866) is poorly documented, and the date of abandonment is approximate.
